questions.question_text:
A solid is a cylinder of radius $4$ cm and height $9$ cm with a cone of the same radius and height $6$ cm on top.
Find its total volume in cm³, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used $\pi r^2 h$ for the cone too, forgetting its factor of one third.
Found only the cylinder and left out the cone.

questions.question_text:
A tank is a cylinder of radius $3$ cm and height $10$ cm capped by a hemisphere of the same radius.
Find its total volume in cm³, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used a full sphere on top instead of a hemisphere.
Found only the cylinder and left out the hemisphere.

questions.question_text:
An ice-cream is a cone of radius $3$ cm and height $8$ cm topped with a hemisphere of the same radius.
Find the total volume in cm³, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used a full sphere on top instead of a hemisphere.
Used $\pi r^2 h$ for the cone, forgetting its factor of one third.

questions.question_text:
An hourglass is two identical cones joined at their points.
Each cone has radius $4$ cm and height $9$ cm.
Find the total volume in cm³, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Found only one cone instead of two.
Left out the factor of one third on each cone.

questions.question_text:
A cone of the same radius and height is drilled out of a solid cylinder of radius $6$ cm and height $10$ cm.
Find the volume of the remaining solid in cm³, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Added the cone instead of subtracting it.
Gave the cone’s volume instead of the remaining solid.

questions.question_text: A square-based pyramid of base side $6$ m and height $9$ m sits on top of a cube of edge $6$ m. Find the total volume of the solid in m³.

options.why: Left out the factor of one third on the pyramid (used $Ah$).
Found only the cube and left out the pyramid.

questions.question_text: A grain silo is a cylinder of radius $1$ m and height $4$ m topped by a cone of the same radius and height $3$ m. Find its capacity in litres, to the nearest litre. ($1$ m³ $= 1000$ L)

options.why: Found only the cylinder and left out the cone roof.
Left out the factor of one third on the cone.

questions.question_text:
A capsule is a cylinder of radius $3$ cm and height $h$ with a hemisphere on each end (together a full sphere).
Its total volume is $63\pi$ cm³.
Find $h$ in cm.

options.why: Ignored the sphere and set the cylinder equal to the whole volume.
Used one hemisphere ($18\pi$) instead of the full sphere for the two caps.

questions.solution_text:
$V_{\text{sphere}} = \frac{4}{3}\pi \times 3^{3} = 36\pi$
$V_{\text{cylinder}} = \pi \times 3^{2} \times h = 9\pi h$
$V_{\text{total}} = 9\pi h + 36\pi$
$63\pi = 9\pi h + 36\pi$
$27\pi = 9\pi h$
$h = 3\text{ cm}$
